What Problem It Addresses: Technical debt and early warning signs created when developers use LLM coding assistants.
What It Proposes or Studies: Conducts a literature review on how AI-assisted coding introduces technical debt.
Multivocal Literature Review (MLR) (31 papers + 73 practitioner sources)
Main Result: Finds that LLMs speed up coding but increase traditional code debt and introduce new debts like prompt debt and fast-integration debt.

What Problem It Addresses: Code completion LLMs recommending deprecated or outdated library APIs.
What It Proposes or Studies: Evaluates why LLMs recommend deprecated APIs and tests ways to fix this behavior.
Empirical Evaluation / Benchmark (145 API mappings across 7 LLMs)
Main Result: Shows that all tested LLMs frequently suggest deprecated APIs because their training data contains older code.

What Problem It Addresses: Lack of knowledge on how developers use and update machine learning libraries in Software 2.0.
What It Proposes or Studies: Large-scale study on ML library adoption, update habits, and developer challenges.
Repository Mining (3,340 GitHub repos) & Developer Survey (109 users)
Main Result: Shows ML library usage grew from 2% to 50% of Python repos; library updates often cause model incompatibility or cascading updates.

What Problem It Addresses: AI code generators failing when generated code must match specific library versions.
What It Proposes or Studies: Benchmarks LLMs on generating version-specific Python code (GitChameleon 2.0).
Main Result: Top AI models score only 48–51%, showing severe difficulty when required to write code for specific library versions.

What Problem It Addresses: Heavy technical debt and rigid architecture in legacy enterprise information systems.
What It Proposes or Studies: Investigates how legacy enterprise systems can be reconfigured successfully.
Main Result: Identifies key organizational and technical mechanisms needed to update legacy enterprise systems.

What Problem It Addresses: Updating deprecated API knowledge in LLMs without expensive full model retraining.
What It Proposes or Studies: Proposes lightweight model editing (AdaLoRA-L) to fix deprecated API outputs in LLMs.
Main Result: Targeted model edits fix deprecated API recommendations while preserving general coding abilities.

What Problem It Addresses: Lack of empirical evidence on Self-Admitted Technical Debt (SATD) in software using LLMs.
What It Proposes or Studies: Mines open-source GitHub projects to analyze prevalence and repayment of LLM-SATD.
Repository Mining (90,845 SATD comments) & Thematic Analysis
Main Result: Creates a taxonomy of 10 categories (e.g., prompt debt, tool calling debt); shows LLM-SATD is repaid faster than regular debt.

What Problem It Addresses: High manual effort needed to migrate old ML code to modern framework versions (e.g., TF 1.x to 2.x).
What It Proposes or Studies: Proposes LLMigrate, an automated pipeline using LLMs and RAG for legacy ML code migration.
System Building & Empirical Evaluation (20 Python files)
Main Result: Automated migration completed 90% of files in 5 minutes compared to 5 days of manual work, removing old session debt.

What Problem It Addresses: Hidden maintenance costs and system-level anti-patterns in production ML systems.
What It Proposes or Studies: Establishes foundational concepts of ML technical debt (glue code, pipeline jungles, feedback loops).
Main Result: Shows that most ML technical debt lives outside model code, in data pipelines, infrastructure, and missing monitors.

What Problem It Addresses: Traditional AI technical debt models failing to capture risks in autonomous agentic AI systems.
What It Proposes or Studies: Maps 31 AI technical debts to agentic manifestations (memory corruption, orchestration fragility).
Main Result: Shows that agent autonomy, persistent memory, and multi-agent coordination turn static pipeline debt into dynamic emergent risks.

What Problem It Addresses: Lack of structured tools to measure technical debt in AI/ML competition platforms.
What It Proposes or Studies: Scoping review of AI technical debt and proposal of an 18-category assessment framework.
Main Result: Categorizes 18 AI technical debt types (including Accessibility Debt) and provides a questionnaire to measure platform debt.

What Problem It Addresses: Algorithm Debt (AD) in ML/DL systems being confused with data or model debt, hurting scalability.
What It Proposes or Studies: Characterizes Algorithm Debt, tests detection models, and gathers practitioner feedback.
Mixed-Methods (SLR of 44 papers, Survey of 65, Interviews with 21)
Main Result: Defines Algorithm Debt as suboptimal algorithmic logic choices; identifies developer knowledge gaps as a main cause and education as top fix.

What Problem It Addresses: Data debt accumulation in AI software lacking alignment with standard lifecycle processes.
What It Proposes or Studies: Maps empirical Data Debt cases to ISO/IEC 5338 and 12207 standards using LLM validation.
Mapping Study & LLM Validation (145 Data Debt cases)
Main Result: Highlights Quality Assurance, Data Engineering, and HR as key process areas to prevent data debt in AI projects.

What Problem It Addresses: Evaluating how well LLMs can refactor complex architectural smells (e.g., Cyclic Dependencies).
What It Proposes or Studies: Compares different prompting methods (detailed vs. simple) and RAG for LLM architectural refactoring.
Main Result: Detailed step-by-step prompts combined with RAG significantly improve LLM refactoring quality for architectural smells.

What Problem It Addresses: Scattered research on technical debt types and anti-patterns specific to AI-based systems.
What It Proposes or Studies: Systematic mapping study classifying AI technical debt, anti-patterns, and quality impacts.
Main Result: Groups AI debt into data, code, model, and infrastructure debts, showing strong negative impact on system maintainability.

What Problem It Addresses: High operational cost, latency, and maintenance debt when deploying LLMs to production.
What It Proposes or Studies: Reviews deployment architectures (RAG vs fine-tuning) and operational debt in LLM systems.
Main Result: Details trade-offs between RAG and fine-tuning regarding infrastructure cost, maintenance effort, and latency debt.

What Problem It Addresses: Technical debt created specifically by prompt engineering choices in LLM codebases.
What It Proposes or Studies: Mines open-source repos to analyze "Prompt Debt" across different prompting techniques.
Main Result: Instruction-based and few-shot prompts create the highest debt due to unclear examples, placeholder stubs, and instruction drift.

What Problem It Addresses: Managing technical debt across shifting paradigms from DevOps to MLOps and GenAIOps.
What It Proposes or Studies: Multivocal literature review tracing technical debt management across DevOps, MLOps, and GenAI.
Main Result: Identifies new GenAI debt types (prompt maintenance, explainability debt) and evaluates AI tools used for debt reduction.

What Problem It Addresses: Lack of detailed understanding of Self-Admitted Technical Debt (SATD) in open-source ML code.
What It Proposes or Studies: Categorizes code comments across open-source ML projects into a 23-type ML SATD taxonomy.
Main Result: ML SATD concentrates heavily in data preprocessing and model evaluation stages, differing from standard software debt.

What Problem It Addresses: Developers ignoring or delaying fixes for deprecated Python library APIs in client code.
What It Proposes or Studies: Tracks how open-source Python projects handle or fail to handle library API deprecations.
Main Result: Developers frequently ignore deprecation warnings, causing runtime crashes and hidden technical debt when libraries update.

What Problem It Addresses: Security vulnerabilities and broken code caused by LLMs recommending outdated library versions.
What It Proposes or Studies: Evaluates LLM library version selection and security vulnerabilities across 1,000 tasks (PinTrace).
Main Result: LLMs frequently recommend older library versions containing known security flaws (CVEs) due to training data recency bias.

What Problem It Addresses: Understanding how developers perform refactoring in machine learning codebases compared to standard code.
What It Proposes or Studies: Analyzes refactoring commits in open-source ML projects using RefactoringMiner.
Main Result: ML refactorings focus heavily on hyperparameter tuning, cleaning data pipelines, and upgrading ML framework versions.

What Problem It Addresses: Understanding maintenance patterns, popularity, and model updates in public model hubs.
What It Proposes or Studies: Analyzes model evolution, commit histories, and discussions across Hugging Face models.
Main Result: Most model activity is concentrated in a few popular organizations; 83.5% of models enter low-maintenance stability after release.

What Problem It Addresses: Lack of clear categorization for deep learning model changes and code evolution over time.
What It Proposes or Studies: Constructs a taxonomy of DL API changes by analyzing model evolution patterns.
Main Result: Categorizes DL changes across data preparation, neural network architecture, hyperparameter tuning, and training loops.

What Problem It Addresses: Evaluating LLM capabilities on complex code migration across different library environment versions.
What It Proposes or Studies: Benchmarks LLMs on finding API changes and rewriting code between old and new environments (CODEMENV).
Main Result: LLMs locate API changes well but struggle significantly with full code rewrites, especially when adapting newer code to older environments.

What Problem It Addresses: Knowledge conflict when an LLM's internal memory contradicts updated external API documentation.
What It Proposes or Studies: Evaluates LLMs prompted with updated API documentation that conflicts with pre-cutoff training weights.
Benchmark Dataset (270 real API updates across 11 LLMs)
Main Result: LLMs often ignore provided documentation and default to outdated memorized API patterns, causing broken code.

What Problem It Addresses: Removing deprecated API knowledge from code LLMs without ruining general coding capabilities.
What It Proposes or Studies: Proposes MUDAPIBench to evaluate machine unlearning methods for removing deprecated API knowledge.
Unlearning Experiment (8 methods across 3 code LLMs)
Main Result: Gradient Difference (GD) unlearning effectively suppresses deprecated API outputs while preserving general code generation quality.

What Problem It Addresses: Maintenance overhead from unused dependencies, broken rules, and dead build targets in large build files.
What It Proposes or Studies: Reports Google's experience and automated tools for detecting and cleaning build debt in BUILD files.
Main Result: Automated build dependency analysis cleans unused targets and significantly improves build speeds in large codebases.

What Problem It Addresses: Empirical prevalence, severity, and refactoring effort of AI technical debt in production systems.
What It Proposes or Studies: Surveys 53 AI practitioners on 9 code and architectural AI technical debt scenarios.
Main Result: Practitioners rate "Deep God Files" and "Jumbled Model Architectures" highest in severity and refactoring effort.

What Problem It Addresses: Detecting Sculley et al.'s hidden technical debt (HTD) patterns during early ML prototyping phases.
What It Proposes or Studies: Case study of an ML public transit predictor and a practitioner workshop using $100-voting.
Main Result: Underutilized data dependencies emerge early in prototyping; practitioners prioritize external world changes as top debt risk.

What Problem It Addresses: Identifying technical debt factors unique to AI-based recommendation systems.
What It Proposes or Studies: Outlines 15 technical debt factors and a research roadmap for AI recommender systems.
Main Result: Establishes a specialized debt agenda covering recommendation feedback loops, cold-start shortcuts, and item staleness.

What Problem It Addresses: Understanding how industrial developers perceive and manage architectural smells in practice.
What It Proposes or Studies: Qualitative study interviewing 21 practitioners across 3 European software companies.
Main Result: Practitioners perceive "God Components" and "Cyclic Dependencies" as the most severe drivers of reduced maintainability.

What Problem It Addresses: Quantifying the financial/effort principal of Architectural Technical Debt (ATD) using objective metrics.
What It Proposes or Studies: Builds the Architectural Technical Debt Index (ATDI) using machine learning (Learning-to-Rank) on architectural smells.
Main Result: Learning-to-Rank models accurately rank smell severity, producing an objective, actionable ATD index weighted by smell extent.
